# WP-29. Remote transport and relay

## Goal

An agent shares a published version to a remote server with one command; the link works while the author's machine sleeps; answers, waits and actions behave exactly as they do locally.

## Owned requirements

Close each with the check below, through the real public interface (README §3).

| ID | Requirement | Route | Concrete check |
|---|---|---|---|
| RM-01 | v1 seams: portable artifact packages, ports for identity, storage and addressing, a worker-isolation interface, a stateless MCP design | M, R | Bundle moves between homes keeping identity; ports and WorkerLauncher documented; MCP server stateless (handle-only test) |
| RM-02 | Remote transport: the host protocol over an authenticated network transport, sign-in from the CLI, sharing a published version to a remote server, and reading waits, results and events back, with remote submissions delivered through the local outbox | I, X | Two instances on one machine, one as a remote server (`mostra-runtime server`): `mostra login` by the device grant, `share --cloud`, open from a browser, submit; the respondent sees "Your answer was sent." and no delivery state (IN-13 for hosted links, D165 item 1a); `wait` returns and the local host receives the delivery exactly once in effect through the owner's outbox; the sync cursor brings signals and state changes to local waits; a push sends only missing files and never server code (grep); a connection silenced past 45 s reconnects; a second instance of the account receives nothing; with two linked instances of one account, the owner instance's host receives each submission once and the other instance receives no delivery and imports nothing; signing out and in again keeps the instance's artifacts; a hosted home whose whole data directory is restored from a lagging copy under traffic, with no restore call, rotates its incarnation when its owner instance reconnects (the owner's committed cursor or relay mark above the home's), continues relay sequences above the owner's mark, drops and logs an update for a run it no longer knows, and gives a viewer resuming above the head a fresh snapshot, and the owner keeps what it imported, follows on and records the regression; an open binding is closed at its token's expiry unless refreshed in band, and within 60 s of a revocation; external: the same against a deployed server |
| RM-04 | Relay: a remote server forwards hosted artifacts' action calls and live producers to the owning instance over its outbound connection; secrets never leave the owner; offline behavior follows the artifact's policy, with a capped queue that drains in order and an outcome-unknown end for a run the owner never reported (D165 item 4); authoring operations are relayed for remote MCP (D165 item 5, MC-04) | I | A counting fake mail action pressed on the hosted page runs once on the owner; owner offline: under `queue` the run waits and runs once on return, in order and at the drain rate, under `fail` it ends at once, and past the cap a run is refused before it is recorded; relay cut mid-run: the owner finishes and reports, past the offline limit the run is `unknown` and the reported end replaces it once; a repeated relay message starts nothing; a grep shows no secret in relay traffic; the owner accepts a run and its acknowledgement is lost: the run is sent again, joins, and happens once; an owner restored to before runs it accepted: they become `unknown` and are never sent again; after every reconnect the accepted, unfinished runs are reconciled before any waiting run drains |
| RM-07 | Counts by choice: an artifact that opts in through its manifest gets a built-in tally of a fixed-choice field, counted in the submit transaction and pushed to viewers on the live channel with no artifact code and no relay, on hosted and local homes alike | I, B | An artifact with a manifest tally: three hundred submissions across three choices give exactly those counts in the hosted home and in a local one, viewers receive them on the live channel with the owner offline and no worker running, a value outside the listed choices counts nothing (so no free text is ever shown), and a count never goes down (trigger) |

## Scope

From [WORK_PACKAGES.md](../WORK_PACKAGES.md):

the owner's side and the server's core of ARCHITECTURE §15 (D165):
- from WP-24: the `bundle` export class, moving a bundle between homes with its version identity, `mostra run <bundle>`, and the `WorkerLauncher` seam documented as the future `SandboxPort` (RM-01);
- `mostra-runtime server`'s core: the data directory and its locks, hosted homes opened on demand and closed when idle, the server's directory ledger, version files over HTTPS, `hosted/push`, and hosted pages routed by exact `Host` (hosted routes with random labels, the shell on the apex) with cookie-free header sessions and worker-mode frames;
- the network binding (JSON-RPC over WebSocket, heartbeats, the message limit, reconnection) and the authorization server's device grant for `mostra login`, with a development identity provider for tests (WP-30 adds the real ones);
- the owner instance as a host of its hosted home: `remote/*`, the submissions port feeding the local outbox, the sync cursor, forwarded state and live writes, one owner instance per artifact and the account's default instance;
- the relay: runs, calls, live producers and server code's effects, the offline policy, the capped queue and its drain, `ownerUnreachable` and `unknown`;
- the respondent's "Your answer was sent." on hosted links (IN-13 as amended);
- the tally (RM-07), locally and hosted;
- the CLI's `login`, `logout`, `share --cloud`, cloud shares in `share list` and `stop`, and links in `status`;
- remote scenarios in the conformance kit, and the Skill and docs for sharing to a server (prose with Mirza, D149).

Design detail for this package:

- WP-28 designed this package's surface (D165, M56): ARCHITECTURE §15, INTERFACES §18, DATA_MODEL §7 and FAILURE_MODEL §11. Build them as written; settle finer shapes under D123 and record each additively in those sections, and bring Mirza any place where the design is wrong or silent.
- From WP-24 (D125): the `bundle` export class, `mostra run <bundle>` and the documentation of `WorkerLauncher` as the future `SandboxPort` move here, because a share pushes the bundle (RM-01). WP-24's VR-07 evidence reuses this bundle.
- From WP-08 (D135): a version's server code imports its packages by name and runs them from the layout of its `lock.yaml` (or the warm set). `mostra run <bundle>` imports a bundle into another home, whose launcher installs the bundle's lockfile into its own layout before the worker starts; the test worker host (`packages/runtime/test/fixtures/worker-host.mjs`) shows the shape. The relay itself doesn't use a remote launcher: relayed runs run in the owner instance's own pool (D165 item 4).
- The server's core (INTERFACES §18.1, DATA_MODEL §7.1, §7.2). `@mostra/runtime` gains the modules `server` (the remote server: its front, hosted homes, the directory ledger, the binding endpoint and the authorization server) and `link` (the owner's side), each with one public `index.ts` (REPO_STANDARDS §3). A hosted home reuses the ledger, interaction, registry, live, actions and gateway route code in a hosted mode with no builder, verify, workers, dependency store or secrets. Its ledger opens in WAL with normal locking and `synchronous=FULL` behind an advisory lock on `home.lock` (D165 item 0b, amending D81 for hosted homes); prove that a second process refuses the home, that a crashed server's lock is released, that a backup replicator (Litestream, as a test tool) reads a live hosted ledger, and that a data directory on a network filesystem is refused. Measure a closed home's open time (target under 250 ms at the 95th percentile) and record it.
- The network binding (INTERFACES §18.2): JSON-RPC over WebSocket at `/host`, one message per text frame up to `MAX_LINE_LENGTH`, pings every 20 s and a 45 s silence limit (prove it with a stand-in proxy that drops idle connections at 60 s), reconnection with backoff, version files over HTTPS (`/files/<sha256>`, only the missing ones), and `hosted/push`, which never stores server files (a grep over the data directory).
- Sign-in: the authorization server's device grant (`/oauth/device`, `/oauth/token`) behind `mostra login`, with a development identity provider for tests; tokens hashed, refresh tokens rotating. WP-30 adds the real identity providers, viewer sign-in and the MCP clients' flows on the same server.
- The owner instance as a host of its hosted home (D165 item 1): `remote/*` methods; the `submissions` port feeding the local outbox in one transaction (imported rows keep their IDs, with `origin`); the sync cursor as a named subscription whose events are copied once each; artifact state and live values forwarded to the hosted home and never applied locally alone; one owner instance per hosted artifact; the account's default instance, the first linked, and a command to change it (this session names it, help drafted with Mirza).
- The relay (INTERFACES §18.3): runs, plain calls, live producers and server code's effects; `waiting` (reserved by WP-08, D130) is entered for the first time; `unknown` joins `action_run`'s states, replaced once by a reported end (a trigger); the offline policy, the capped queue and its drain rate; `ownerUnreachable`. Prove every row of FAILURE_MODEL §11.1 with a counting fake mail server, including a relay cut mid-run, a crash of the owner mid-run and a repeated relay message.
- After the Claude Opus review of WP-28 (D165's refinements): hosted routes (`rte_` IDs and random labels, keyed by home and artifact, every issued label recorded forever, the shell's paths `/a/<routeId>`); a submission's one delivery owner is its artifact's owner link, and `HomeConfig.ports` is kept per link on a hosted home; `relay_run.accepted_at`, `port/relay.reconcile` after every reconnect and the owner's `relayMark`; a hosted home's incarnation, rotated on a restore, and an owner that continues after the restored head and records `remote.regressed`; the instance's `lnk_` ID kept across `logout` (unless `--forget`) and rebound at sign-in; in-band token refresh (`remote/token`) and closing a binding at its token's expiry; a JSON-RPC heartbeat beside the pings; each lock a one-row SQLite database in exclusive locking; version files present for a home only through its own uploads and versions, uploads only for a pending push, references counted with pushes and removals; the device page's warning and `instance.linked`. After its second review: the owner instance as the witness of a hosted home's restore (its committed cursor and relay mark in `mostra/initialize`), `mostra-runtime server --restored`, relay sequences continuing above the owner's mark and unique per link, reconciling before the waiting runs drain, `home_file` rows only from uploads or complete versions, and one artifact shared to several servers. Each has its row in FAILURE_MODEL §11 and its part of RM-02's or RM-04's check.
- On hosted links a respondent sees "Your answer was sent." once the hosted home commits, and no delivery state, which the owner sees (D165 item 1a, amending IN-13 for hosted links); prove both in a browser. The viewer-facing wording is accepted with the package's prose (D149).
- The tally (RM-07, D165 item 12): the manifest's `tally`, the `tally` table written only in the submit transaction, and the live key `$tally/<field>`, on local and hosted homes alike.
- Remote submissions reach the host through the local outbox, so H-04's guarantees (durable before delivery, ordered, idempotent replay) hold for hosted artifacts too; add remote scenarios to the conformance kit (a local host whose instance shares to a server the kit runs).
- CLI (INTERFACES §18.7): `mostra login`, `logout`, `share --cloud` and cloud shares in `share list` and `stop`, links in `status`; their help, the new diagnostics' hints and the Skill's sharing reference (the `hosted` manifest keys, `tally`, `useViewer`'s new sources, `useAction`'s `waiting` and `unknown`) are drafted with Mirza and accepted in one batch (D149).
- Open issues on the `WP-29` milestone (work-package protocol §2, M41), each fixed at its root with a test as strict as before, or closed with evidence: #114 (`mostra open` run by an agent opens no browser and doesn't say so, while the Skill says it opens), #116 (the Skill has no pattern for an approval whose button does something, so agents drop the submission), #118 (under `epochs` a new round still shows the last round's "Submitted" card), #119 (over a quick tunnel an action's result reaches the page about 20 s late, which hosted pages behind a buffering edge would meet too). Each touches code this package changes: the CLI and the Skill's references, the shell's after-submit card, and run updates over polls.
- Secrets never cross the relay: grep tests over relay traffic, as WP-08's over logs and events. Keep the Windows legs green: the owner's side runs on every platform, and the server's suites run on all three too.

## Out of scope

- Viewer sign-in, identity providers, the full authorization server, operator ports, the hosted shell's trusted chrome, anonymous answers at volume, pause, remote MCP and the container image (WP-30)
- Sandboxed remote execution (RM-06, v1.x)
- Team features (WP-31)
- Moving an artifact to another owner instance (additive later, D165 item 1b)

## Acceptance evidence

RM-01's check (including a bundle that moves between two homes and keeps its version identity), RM-02's, RM-04's and RM-07's, against a real `mostra-runtime server` on the same machine.

Also: `pnpm check` green, diff reviewed, the progress report's evidence table complete for every owned requirement (README §3), the evidence matrix regenerated, docs and AGENTS.md current, and the report finalized after acceptance (README §4).

## Risks and notes

- Exactly once in effect across two ledgers: every relayed call and every synced submission carries a stable ID end to end (FAILURE_MODEL §1 rule 3).
- Secrets never cross the relay: grep tests over relay traffic, as WP-08's over logs and events.
- The scope is broad; if it can't finish in one session, continue under the recovery rule with the same identity and scope (STANDARDS continuation). If it runs long, the tally (RM-07) is the piece that moves to WP-30 most cleanly, with Mirza's agreement and a change to WORK_PACKAGES.md.

## Handoff

Hosted links whose answers and actions flow back to the owner, served by a real `mostra-runtime server`; WP-30 makes it the public server.
